raw_text:
Here’s a 12-week muscle gain program tailored for a 26-year-old recreational lifter, strict vegan, with access to a full gym. It includes a structured training plan (3 phases), weekly progression, and a vegan nutrition plan targeting 150 g protein/day.

Program overview
- Goal: Hypertrophy (lean mass gain) with progressive overload
- Duration: 12 weeks, split into 3 phases (4 weeks each)
- Training frequency: 4 days/week (Upper/Lower split), optional 5th day for accessories/conditioning
- Progression: Double progression within rep ranges; add load when top of range is met across sets
- Intensity: RPE 7–9 across main lifts, deload in Week 4 and Week 8
- Cardio: 2 light sessions/week (20–25 min Zone 2), primarily for recovery and appetite
- Recovery: 7–9 hours sleep, 1–2 rest days/week, mobility where noted

Phase structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation hypertrophy and movement quality. Moderate volume, learning rep tempos, establish baseline loads. Week 4 deload.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Volume/overload emphasis. Slight volume increase, more sets near failure. Week 8 deload.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Intensification and specialization. Heavier top sets, back-off volume, add advanced techniques (rest-pause, myo-reps) selectively.

Weekly split
- Day 1: Upper A (Push emphasis)
- Day 2: Lower A (Squat/quad emphasis)
- Day 3: Rest or cardio/mobility
- Day 4: Upper B (Pull/shoulders emphasis)
- Day 5: Lower B (Hinge/glute-ham emphasis)
- Day 6: Optional accessories/conditioning (arms, calves, core, light cardio) or rest
- Day 7: Rest

General guidelines
- Warm-up: 5–8 min light cardio + dynamic mobility; 2–3 specific warm-up sets per main lift
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 s), brief pause where noted, strong concentric
- Rest: 90–150 s for compounds; 60–90 s for accessories; 30–45 s for isolation supersets
- Progression: When you hit the top of the rep range across all working sets with good form, increase load by 2–5% next session
- RPE: Aim RPE 7–8 for most sets; final set of key accessories can reach RPE 9 in Phases 2–3

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Focus: Technique, mind-muscle connection, consistent volume. Deload in Week 4 (reduce sets by ~40% and stop 3 reps shy of failure).

Week 1
- Upper A
  - Barbell flat bench press 3×6–8 (RPE 7–8)
  - Seated DB shoulder press 3×8–10
  - Incline DB press 3×8–10
  - Chest-supported row 3×8–10
  - Lat pulldown (medium grip) 3×8–12
  - Cable lateral raise 3×12–15
  - Triceps rope pressdown 3×10–12
- Lower A
  - Back squat 3×6–8
  - Romanian deadlift 3×8–10
  - Leg press (feet mid-high) 3×10–12
  - Bulgarian split squat 3×8–10/leg
  - Seated calf raise 3×10–15
  - Hanging leg raise or reverse crunch 3×10–15
- Upper B
  - Weighted pull-up or assisted pull-up 3×5–8
  - One-arm DB row 3×8–10/side
  - Overhead press (barbell) 3×5–8
  - High-incline DB press 3×8–10
  - Face pull 3×12–15
  - Cable rear delt fly 3×12–15
  - EZ-bar curl 3×8–12
- Lower B
  - Deadlift (conventional or sumo) 3×4–6 (RPE 7)
  - Front squat or hack squat 3×6–8
  - Hip thrust 3×8–10
  - Leg curl (lying or seated) 3×10–12
  - Standing calf raise 3×10–15
  - Cable woodchop or Pallof press 3×12–15/side

Week 2
- Same exercises. Aim to add 1–2 reps per set or small load increases. Keep RPE 7–8.

Week 3
- Same structure. Push most compounds to top of rep ranges at RPE 8.

Week 4 (Deload)
- Reduce sets by ~40% (e.g., 2 sets for most), keep RPE ~6–7, maintain technique. No AMRAPs or grinders.

Phase 2: Overload (Weeks 5–8)
Increase volume (add 1 set to main lifts/isolation), use some near-failure sets. Deload in Week 8.

Week 5
- Upper A
  - Barbell flat bench press 4×6–8
  - Seated DB shoulder press 4×8–10
  - Incline DB press 3×8–10
  - Chest-supported row 4×8–10
  - Lat pulldown (wide-neutral) 3×8–12
  - Cable lateral raise 4×12–15 (last set RPE 9)
  - Triceps rope pressdown 3×10–12 + 1 drop set
- Lower A
  - Back squat 4×6–8
  - Romanian deadlift 4×8–10
  - Leg press 4×10–12 (short lockout, constant tension)
  - Bulgarian split squat 3×8–10/leg
  - Seated calf raise 4×10–15
  - Weighted decline crunch 3×12–15
- Upper B
  - Weighted pull-up 4×5–8
  - One-arm DB row 4×8–10/side
  - Overhead press 4×5–8
  - High-incline DB press 3×8–10
  - Face pull 3×12–15
  - Cable rear delt fly 3×12–15
  - EZ-bar curl 3×8–12 + 1 myo-rep cluster (e.g., 12 + 3+3+3)
- Lower B
  - Deadlift 4×3–5 (RPE 7–8, leave 2 reps in reserve)
  - Front squat or hack squat 4×6–8
  - Barbell hip thrust 4×8–10 (2 s squeeze at top)
  - Leg curl 4×10–12
  - Standing calf raise 4×10–15
  - Cable woodchop 3×12–15/side

Week 6
- Progress loads/reps where possible; push last isolation set to RPE 9. Keep compounds at RPE 8–9 on final set.

Week 7
- Keep sets identical; try to hit top of ranges. One advanced technique per session max (drop set or myo-reps on an isolation movement).

Week 8 (Deload)
- Reduce sets by ~50%, keep RPE 6–7. Maintain movement patterns, skip advanced techniques.

Phase 3: Intensification & Specialization (Weeks 9–12)
Slightly heavier top sets with back-off volume; add glute/shoulder/upper-back emphasis for aesthetics.

Week 9
- Upper A
  - Bench press: top set 1×5–6 (RPE 8) + back-off 3×6–8 (-10% load)
  - Seated DB shoulder press 3×8–10
  - Incline DB press 3×8–10
  - Chest-supported row: top set 1×6–8 + back-off 2×8–10
  - Lat pulldown 3×8–12
  - Cable lateral raise 4×12–15 (rest-pause on last set)
  - Overhead cable triceps extension 3×10–12
- Lower A
  - Back squat: top set 1×5–6 (RPE 8) + back-off 3×6–8
  - Romanian deadlift 3×6–8 (slightly heavier than Phase 2)
  - Leg press 3×10–12
  - Walking lunge 3×10–12/leg
  - Seated calf raise 4×8–12 (2 s pause stretch at bottom)
  - Ab wheel rollout 3×8–12
- Upper B
  - Weighted pull-up: top set 1×4–6 + back-off 3×6–8
  - Overhead press: top set 1×4–6 + back-off 3×6–8
  - One-arm DB row 3×8–10/side
  - Cable/machine rear delt row 3×12–15
  - Incline cable fly 3×12–15
  - Alternating DB curl 3×10–12
- Lower B
  - Deadlift: top set 1×3–4 (RPE 8) + back-off 2×4–6 (-10–12%)
  - Front squat or hack squat 3×6–8
  - Barbell hip thrust 4×6–8 (heavier)
  - Seated or lying leg curl 3×8–10
  - Standing calf raise 4×8–12
  - Weighted side plank 3×30–45 s/side

Week 10
- Aim small load increases on top sets; match or beat back-off volume. Keep form strict.

Week 11
- Final push week. One isolation movement per day can use rest-pause or myo-reps. Compounds stay at RPE 8–9; avoid true failure.

Week 12 (Consolidation)
- Keep structure, but stop all sets 2 reps shy of failure (RPE ~8). Focus on crisp execution, set up for next training block.

Optional Day 6 (Weeks 2–11, if recovery is good; skip on deloads)
- Arms/Delts/Core finisher (30–40 min, pump work)
  - Cable lateral raise 3×15–20
  - Rope pressdown 3×12–15
  - Cable curl 3×12–15
  - Machine rear delt 3×15–20
  - Hanging knee raise 3×12–15
- OR 20–25 min Zone 2 cardio + 10 min mobility

Cardio and mobility
- 2×/week 20–25 min Zone 2 (easy conversational pace), ideally on rest days
- 10–12 min mobility flow after training: hips, T-spine, shoulders, ankles
- Steps: 7–10k/day to support recovery and appetite

Nutrition plan (strict vegan, 150 g protein/day)
Calorie target
- Start at ~200–300 kcal/day surplus above maintenance. For a 26-year-old recreational lifter, a rough starting point is 32–36 kcal/kg. Example: at 65 kg, ~2,100–2,350 kcal maintenance; start ~2,350–2,650 kcal/day. Adjust by +/–150–200 kcal based on 0.25–0.5 kg/month weight gain and gym performance.

Macros
- Protein: 150 g/day (2.0–2.3 g/kg if 60–75 kg), from plants only
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg (e.g., 50–70 g/day)
- Carbs: remainder (typically 275–375 g/day depending on calories)
- Fiber: 25–40 g/day (don’t overdo to protect appetite)

Protein quality strategy
- Prioritize complete or complementary proteins:
  - Soy (tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk, soy yogurt)
  - Seitan (vital wheat gluten; avoid if gluten-sensitive)
  - Legume + grain combos (rice + beans, lentils + quinoa, hummus + pita)
  - Buckwheat, quinoa, amaranth (higher lysine)
  - Plant protein powders: soy isolate, pea + rice blend; aim 1–2 scoops/day
- Leucine: target ~2.5–3.0 g leucine per meal for MPS. Practically, 30–40 g high-quality plant protein per meal or use blends/fortified powders.

Meal timing
- 4–5 protein feedings/day, spaced 3–4 hours
- Pre-workout: carbs + some protein 60–90 min before
- Post-workout: 30–40 g plant protein (shake or meal) within 1–2 hours + 60–90 g carbs
- Evening: protein serving before bed (soy yogurt, tofu bowl, or shake)

Sample 1-day vegan meal plan (~2,500–2,700 kcal, 150 g protein)
- Breakfast
  - Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu) with veggies + 2 slices whole-grain toast
  - Soy milk (300 ml)
  - Fruit (banana or berries)
  - Protein: ~45 g; Carbs: ~70 g; Fat: ~15 g
- Snack (pre-workout if training AM)
  - Soy isolate or pea/rice blend shake (1.5 scoops = ~35 g protein)
  - Oats (60 g) with maple syrup/cinnamon
  - Protein: ~35 g; Carbs: ~45 g; Fat: ~5 g
- Lunch
  - Lentil-quinoa bowl: cooked lentils (200 g), cooked quinoa (150 g), mixed greens, olive oil/tahini dressing, roasted veggies
  - Protein: ~35 g; Carbs: ~85 g; Fat: ~18 g
- Post-workout or Afternoon snack
  - Tempeh sandwich: tempeh (150 g), whole-grain bread (2–3 slices), lettuce/tomato/mustard; side of edamame (150 g)
  - Protein: ~40 g; Carbs: ~60 g; Fat: ~15 g
- Dinner
  - Seitan stir-fry: seitan (150–180 g) with rice (200 g cooked) and mixed veggies; cashews (15 g)
  - Protein: ~35 g; Carbs: ~80 g; Fat: ~15 g
- Optional evening add-on (if calories needed)
  - Soy yogurt (150–200 g) with granola (30 g)
  - Protein: ~12–15 g; Carbs: ~30 g; Fat: ~6 g

Swaps and convenience options
- High-protein vegan staples: smoked tofu, extra-firm tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame/soybeans, lupini beans, lentils, chickpeas, black beans, mung beans
- Ready items: high-protein soy yogurt, fortified soy milk (8+ g/250 ml), protein pasta, legume-based pasta, tofu noodles
- Snacks: roasted edamame, lupini cups, jerky-style seitan, protein bars (vegan), rice cakes with powdered peanut butter + soy yogurt
- Protein powders: aim for 25–40 g per serving; pea + rice blend improves amino profile

Micronutrients and vegan supplements
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day (vegan-sourced). Safe and effective for muscle/strength.
- Beta-alanine: 3.2–6.4 g/day split doses (optional; supports higher-rep work).
- Omega-3: Algae-based DHA/EPA 250–500 mg/day.
- Vitamin B12: 1,000 mcg cyanocobalamin 2–3×/week or 250 mcg/day.
- Vitamin D3 (vegan): 1,000–2,000 IU/day (adjust with bloodwork/season).
- Iodine: from iodized salt or 150 mcg supplement if intake is low.
- Iron: monitor ferritin; ensure legumes, greens, fortified cereals; pair with vitamin C. Supplement only if bloodwork indicates.
- Calcium: 1,000 mg/day from fortified plant milks/tofu set with calcium sulfate, greens; supplement if dietary intake is low.
- Zinc: include legumes, nuts/seeds; consider 8–12 mg/day if intake is low.

Hydration
- 30–35 ml/kg/day water baseline; +500–1,000 ml around training
- Add electrolytes on long/hot sessions

Bodyweight and progression checks
- Weigh 3×/week, morning, average it; aim for ~0.25–0.5 kg/month gain
- If weight is flat for 2 weeks and performance stalls, add ~150–200 kcal/day (mostly carbs)
- If appetite is low, lower fiber at some meals (use white rice/bread, peeled fruit)

Recovery
- Sleep: 7–9 hours nightly; consistent schedule
- Stress: 5–10 min daily breathwork or light walking
- Deloads: Weeks 4 and 8 as programmed
- Soft tissue: optional 5–10 min foam rolling for quads, glutes, lats post-session

Week-by-week snapshot
- Week 1: Establish loads, technique focus
- Week 2: Add reps where possible
- Week 3: Push to top of ranges (RPE 8)
- Week 4: Deload (–40% sets, RPE 6–7)
- Week 5: Volume bump; add 1 set to key lifts
- Week 6: Slight load increases; one isolation near-failure
- Week 7: Hit top of ranges; one technique (drop/myo) per session
- Week 8: Deload (–50% sets)
- Week 9: Top-set + back-off structure begins
- Week 10: Small load PRs on top sets
- Week 11: Final overload; isolation intensity techniques allowed
- Week 12: Consolidate; stop 2 reps short of failure; prepare for next block

Notes for coaching
- Track RPE, loads, and reps; use double progression
- Watch elbow/shoulder tolerance with pressing; rotate grips if needed
- If deadlift recovery is tough, swap one week for trap bar or reduce back-off volume
- For glute emphasis, you may swap walking lunges for step-ups or add abduction machine 2×/week (3×12–15)
- If time-crunched, keep compounds + 2 accessories; move isolation to Day 6

This plan delivers progressive hypertrophy training with recovery built in and a vegan nutrition framework that reliably hits 150 g protein/day while supporting lean mass gain.
